html_en:
The AI industry is rapidly pivoting from building tools for humans to building tools for agents, while simultaneously discovering that agents make exceptional coding partners.

The Agent-First Development Revolution

Guillermo Rauch crystallized a fundamental shift happening in developer tools:
"We used to build tools for humans, now we're building them for agents."
His announcement that Vercel Labs is hiring to build "the devtools of the AI era" comes with impressive metrics — their agent-focused tools have garnered 22.8M+ downloads. This isn't just theory anymore. Dan Shipper is coining new terminology for this paradigm shift, proposing "Codex-native" or "Cursor-native" to describe
"apps designed to be used inside of the in-app browser of your agent of choice. the agent can use it and you can use it too, full context is shared, and you can both see what the other is doing."
The practical benefits are already evident. Shipper reports that browsing PostHog inside Codex creates
"SO MUCH better"
collaboration, where
"codex can write queries and see the results, and it makes our collaboration extremely seamless."

Agents as Quality Assurance Partners

Perhaps the most compelling demonstration of agent-human collaboration comes from Peter Steinberger, who has implemented an automated code review system that would make any engineering manager jealous. His setup now runs a codex instance on every commit, and when issues are found,
"a new codex spins up and (if still relevant) makes a PR for the fix. Then a review agent spins up. If an issue is found, another agent will fix the issues. (up to 5 loops)"
The system is already proving its worth — within 10 minutes of going live, it found one of Steinberger's own bugs. This represents a profound shift from agents as assistants to agents as vigilant quality partners. Meanwhile, @trq212 from Anthropic is taking a more targeted approach, hunting down "the most annoying bugs in Claude Code" and asking users to share their "white whales" — those persistent, maddening issues that have evaded fixes.

Solo Builders in the AI Era

Peter Yang's observation that "The world is their playground now" for solo AI builders captures something profound about this moment. Aaron Levie expands on this theme, arguing that "Agents are the single biggest form of leverage for anyone technical in history. Probably has never been a better time to be technical." But Levie offers an important nuance: while agentic coding is
"great for IT people to build vastly more custom systems internally, great for domain experts that want to automate workflows... What it's less great for is casually building complex software that you have to maintain on an ongoing basis."
The key insight? We're going to get "100X more software and vastly more software developers in the future. But that's different from *everyone* rolling their own."

Creative Tools Get the Agent Treatment

Claude made a significant push into creative workflows today, announcing connectors for professional creative tools including Blender, Autodesk Fusion, Adobe Creative Cloud, and Canva. The Autodesk Fusion connector particularly stands out, allowing designers and engineers to
"create and modify 3D models through conversation."
This represents more than feature expansion — it's validation that conversational interfaces are becoming the preferred way professionals want to interact with complex creative software. Zara Zhang captures this shift perfectly, noting she now shares GitHub repos instead of building GUIs,
"Kind of like Karpathy's 'idea file': just write down the idea, and people's agents can build it for them in a customized way."
As Garry Tan wryly noted, if you're "sick of hearing about agents 2026 is going to be the eternal September for you." The agent era isn't coming — it's here, and it's reshaping how we build, test, and collaborate with software in ways we're only beginning to understand.
html_zh:
今天AI圈的一个主题很清晰：我们正在从为人类构建工具转向为AI智能体构建工具，而这种转变正在重塑整个软件开发格局。

🔧 AI时代的开发工具革命

Guillermo Rauch 在宣布Vercel Labs团队扩张时，清晰地表达了这一转变：

我们的使命是构建AI时代的开发工具。我们过去为人类构建工具，现在我们正在为智能体构建它们。@ctatedev和团队已经推出了智能体喜爱的工具：agent-browser、portless、skills、chat、just-bash、json-render...迄今为止已有2280万次下载。

Dan Shipper 进一步探讨了这种"原生"概念，提出需要为智能体时代设计的应用程序：

我们可能需要创造一个新术语：Codex-native、Cowork-native、Cursor-native。这些应用程序专为在你选择的智能体的应用内浏览器中使用而设计。智能体可以使用它，你也可以使用它，完全共享上下文，你们都能看到对方在做什么。在这里构建软件有巨大的机会。

🎨 创意工具的AI整合浪潮

Anthropic今天宣布了一系列重大的连接器更新，显示AI正在深入渗透创意专业领域。Claude AI 发布了对Blender的连接器：

Claude现在连接到创意专业人士已经在使用的工具。通过新的Blender连接器，你可以直接从Claude调试场景、构建新工具，或批量应用更改到每个对象上。

此外，还推出了Adobe Creative Cloud、Ableton、Splice、Canva Affinity、SketchUp和Resolume的连接器。特别值得注意的是，Anthropic还加入了Blender开发基金作为赞助者，支持开源软件的开发。

Zara Zhang 分享了一个有趣的创意工作流程洞察：不要让AI生成图像，而是让它生成SVG！这样可以创建"无缝融入设计风格的矢量插图"。

🤖 智能体驱动的开发实践

一些开发者正在将智能体深度整合到他们的日常工作流程中。Stefan Saasen 展示了一个令人印象深刻的自动化流程：

codex现在在我们提交的每次代码上运行，审查代码 - 如果发现错误，一个新的codex会启动，如果仍然相关，会为修复创建一个PR。然后审查智能体启动。如果发现问题，另一个智能体会修复问题。（最多5个循环）

Dan Shipper 也分享了在Codex中使用PostHog的体验："在codex内部浏览posthog比在浏览器中使用智能体要好得多"，因为codex可以编写查询并查看结果，使协作变得极其无缝。

🎮 用游戏衡量AI能力的新视角

Peter Yang 提出了一个有趣的AI能力评估框架：通过AI模型能够一次性完成或在30分钟内构建的游戏时代来衡量其能力：

如果我们通过AI模型能够一次性完成单个关卡（或用30分钟工作构建）的游戏时代来衡量其优秀程度会如何：Atari、NES、SNES/Sega Genesis、PlayStation/N64、PS2/Xbox/GameCube/Dreamcast、Xbox 360/PS3/Wii、PS4/Xbox One/Switch、PS5/Xbox Series X/S。我认为我们仍然处在NES时代？

Yang还表达了对独立AI构建者的敬意："现在世界就是他们的游乐场。"

💼 软件开发的未来：扩展而非替代

Aaron Levie 对AI对软件工作影响的看法特别发人深省。他强调：

软件工作不会消失。智能体是历史上任何技术人员最大的杠杆形式。从个人、团队或公司角度来看，现在可能是成为技术人员的最佳时机...我们即将体验到比以前多100倍的软件。

Levie进一步解释说，虽然智能体编程对想要完成更多工作的软件开发者来说是巨大的福音，但"对于随意构建你必须持续维护并承担所有风险的复杂软件来说，它就不那么理想了"。

与此同时，Sam Altman 继续在推特上发布神秘的更新预告，暗示OpenAI即将推出重大功能。

今天的动态显示，我们正处在一个转折点：AI不仅在改变我们构建软件的方式，更在重新定义软件本身的概念。从为智能体原生设计的工具，到创意专业领域的深度整合，再到完全自动化的代码审查循环，AI正在从实验阶段迅速进入生产环境的核心。
